instruction: Open system settings and set the automatic screen lock to activate after 5 minutes.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting the screen lock delay to 5 minutes (300 seconds). The evaluator uses gsettings to read the lock-delay value and expects it to be 'uint32 300\n' (5 minutes). Similar to the original task which checks idle-delay setting.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: Uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-delay' which directly reads the screen lock delay setting from GNOME system settings
Metric comparison is correct: exact_match properly compares the command output against the expected value 'uint32 300\n'
Expected value is semantically correct: 5 minutes = 300 seconds, and the format 'uint32 300\n' matches the exact gsettings output format including the trailing newline
Complete instruction coverage: The evaluator verifies the lock-delay setting which is precisely what the instruction requires
Practical feasibility: gsettings command is available on GNOME/Ubuntu systems, doesn't require UI state, and the setting persists after being set
No postconfig needed: The setting can be verified after task completion without reopening any dialogs
